items.title: Finite complex-array norms used by the NUFFT certificates
items.statement: Define the finite complex-array l1, Euclidean, and maximum norms, including value zero on the empty index set.
items.strategy: Give explicit finite-sum/max formulas and state the empty-set convention.

items.title: Periodized Gaussian gridding kernel
items.statement: For tau>0 define the period-one Gaussian sum phi_tau(x)=sum_n exp(-pi(x+n)^2/tau); local convergence and continuity are established by a same-page lemma.
items.strategy: Use Gaussian decay and an explicit geometric majorant on each compact interval.

items.title: Triangle inequality for the finite NUFFT Euclidean norm
items.statement: For finite complex arrays, the counting Euclidean norm satisfies the triangle inequality.
items.strategy: Prove finite-array Cauchy–Schwarz by expanding a nonnegative squared norm, then expand the norm of a sum.

items.title: Type-1, type-2, and type-3 nonuniform Fourier transforms
items.statement: Fix the normalized torus, finite source and mode sets, signs, scaling, type-3 frequency lists, and the exact finite-sum conventions used by the page.
items.strategy: Define each finite matrix explicitly and prove the type-2 formula is its conjugate transpose by finite expansion.

items.title: Local uniform convergence of the periodized Gaussian
items.statement: The Gaussian periodization converges absolutely and locally uniformly, defines a continuous function, and is one-periodic, without a choice axiom.
items.strategy: On each compact interval bound both tails by a convergent geometric series, then prove continuity by a uniform-tail epsilon argument.

items.title: Explicit tail for the periodized Gaussian image sum
items.statement: A finite image sum on [0,1] encloses the periodized Gaussian after adding an explicit two-sided geometric remainder.
items.strategy: Split the positive and negative omitted indices and bound each tail by a geometric series.

items.title: Fourier series of the periodized Gaussian
items.statement: Under Countable Choice, the periodized Gaussian has Fourier coefficients sqrt(tau) exp(-pi tau r^2), and its absolutely convergent Fourier series equals the kernel.
items.strategy: Show the underlying Gaussian is Schwartz, apply the inspected Schwartz Poisson-summation theorem, and substitute the exact two-pi Gaussian transform.
items.axiom_base: Countable Choice is required by the Schwartz Poisson-summation and Gaussian Fourier-transform suppliers.

items.title: Explicit periodized Gaussian spread-tail bound
items.statement: Truncating each coordinate spread to the 2w+1 nearest periodic grid points has a uniform Gaussian-tail bound; the total omitted product-kernel mass is bounded by a coordinatewise union estimate.
items.strategy: Reindex periodic grid sums by the integer lattice, apply a shifted Gaussian tail comparison, and sum the complement of a product neighborhood by a union bound.

items.title: Exact Gaussian grid alias identity and explicit alias bound
items.statement: For a rectangular power-of-two grid with M_r>2K_r, the normalized grid DFT deconvolves to the type-1 sum plus an absolutely convergent alias series bounded by ||c||_1 times a finite product of explicit geometric terms.
items.strategy: Substitute the absolutely convergent kernel Fourier series, use the finite root-of-unity sum coordinatewise, and bound nonzero signed aliases by a geometric series.
items.axiom_base: Countable Choice is inherited from the local Gaussian periodization Fourier-series lemma.

items.title: Certified Gaussian gridding for type 1 and type 2
items.statement: Search a finite list of positive rational Gaussian parameters, power-of-two oversampled grids, and widths; use outward elementary-function enclosures, spreading, unitary axis FFTs, mode deconvolution, explicit analytic error bounds, and conservative failure statuses.
items.strategy: Use the exact alias identity and product Gaussian tail, certify kernel and denominator enclosures, and transfer the published radix-two FFT norm error through interval deconvolution.
items.axiom_base: The certificate branch carries Countable Choice through the local Schwartz Poisson-summation supplier.

items.title: Certified type-1 Gaussian gridding error and type-2 adjoint bound
items.statement: For a successful algorithm result, type 1 has an explicit l-infinity error bounded by an analytic alias-plus-tail term times ||c||_1 and a computed outward rounding radius; the matching type-2 matrix is the conjugate transpose and has the analogous l-infinity bound.
items.strategy: Bound exact grid aliases and omitted spreading, enclose the finite-precision FFT and interval deconvolution, then use the entrywise matrix bound to transfer the same analytic constant to the adjoint.
items.axiom_base: Countable Choice is inherited through the local Schwartz Poisson-summation supplier.

items.title: Exact MRI Fourier samples from a two-point object
items.statement: A two-point weighted object with an off-grid source has exact type-1 Fourier samples given by the stated finite sum, illustrating the discrete MRI k-space model.
items.strategy: Substitute the explicit source locations and coefficients into the type-1 definition and evaluate the zero mode exactly.

items.title: A positive mode multiplier too small to certify
items.statement: A concrete finite dyadic format and Gaussian mode have a strictly positive exact deconvolution multiplier below the smallest positive subnormal, forcing the interval branch to return inconclusive.
items.strategy: Compare the exact positive multiplier with the least subnormal using a lower bound for pi and the positive exponential series.

items.title: Clustered sources and absolute l1 error
items.statement: Two nearby sources with opposite coefficients have fixed coefficient l1 norm while a selected Fourier coefficient tends to zero, so the proved estimate is absolute and supplies no relative-error guarantee.
items.strategy: Compute the exact two-source sum and bound its small exponential difference with the sine and cosine derivative formulas.
